# area: typevartuple_unpack
# hypothesis: A TypeVarTuple captures the exact element types of its arguments, including when a variadic tuple is star-unpacked at the call site, so checkers should keep per-element types rather than widening to tuple[object, ...].
from typing import Generic, TypeVarTuple, Unpack, assert_type, reveal_type

Ts = TypeVarTuple('Ts')


def pack(*args: *Ts) -> tuple[*Ts]:
    return args


def first_then_pack(x: int, *args: Unpack[Ts]) -> tuple[int, *Ts]:
    return (x, *args)


class Box(Generic[*Ts]):
    def __init__(self, *items: *Ts) -> None:
        self.items = items

    def get(self) -> tuple[*Ts]:
        return self.items


p = pack(1, 'a', 2.5)
reveal_type(p)
assert_type(p, tuple[int, str, float])
e = pack()
assert_type(e, tuple[()])
assert e == ()
q = first_then_pack(1, 'a', None)
assert_type(q, tuple[int, str, None])
assert q == (1, 'a', None)
pair = (1, 'a')
r = first_then_pack(*pair)
assert_type(r, tuple[int, str])
b = Box(1, 'x')
reveal_type(b)
assert_type(b, Box[int, str])
assert b.get() == (1, 'x')
bad = first_then_pack('no', 1)  # expect-error
assert bad == ('no', 1)
hypothesis: A TypeVarTuple captures the exact element types of its arguments, including when a variadic tuple is star-unpacked at the call site, so checkers should keep per-element types rather than widening to tuple[object, ...].
